title: AI optical interconnect demand is turning into a multi-layer InP capacity cycle
summary: The 2026 signal now clears the trend gate: demand commitments, device-fab expansions, substrate capacity and commercial epiwafer production are moving in the same direction across separate companies. NVIDIA signed multiyear optics purchase/capacity agreements with Coherent and Lumentum in March; Lumentum is building a 6-inch InP line, Coherent is quadrupling wafer capacity in Sherman, JX Advanced Metals plans up to ¥120 billion to lift Japanese InP substrate capacity roughly 7–10x FY2025, and Sumitomo Chemical has now started mass-producing and selling 4-inch InP epiwafers in Ibaraki. The pattern is real capacity commitment—not proof that every announced wafer will be absorbed profitably.
why_it_matters: AI infrastructure is creating manufacturing demand beyond GPUs: optical links need lasers, modulators, detectors and packaging to move data at high bandwidth without an unsustainable power penalty. For Japan, the notable development is upstream depth: JX is scaling InP substrates while Sumitomo has crossed into commercial InP epitaxy. Globally, device makers are simultaneously adding 6-inch InP fabrication. The caveat is important: these companies are responding to a common AI-networking demand thesis, not necessarily to independent end-markets, and competing optical architectures can change how much InP content ultimately wins.

claims.text: On March 2, NVIDIA announced separate nonexclusive multiyear optics agreements with Coherent and Lumentum; each included a multibillion-dollar purchase commitment/capacity-access arrangement and a $2 billion NVIDIA investment in the supplier.
Lumentum announced a 240,000-square-foot Greensboro facility using 6-inch InP wafers, with NVIDIA as a customer and production ramp expected in mid-2028.
Coherent announced that its Sherman 6-inch InP expansion is intended to double manufacturing production space and quadruple wafer production capacity.
JX Advanced Metals plans up to ¥120 billion of InP-substrate investment over four years and targets production capacity roughly 7–10 times FY2025 levels, with additional capacity in Hitachinaka.
claims.basis: JX Advanced Metals official investment policy

claims.text: Sumitomo Chemical has established mass production of 4-inch InP epitaxial wafers at its Ibaraki Works in Hitachi and has begun commercial sales.

Coherent is simultaneously developing multiple optical architectures and products—including InP lasers, modulators and photodiodes for pluggable, co-packaged and silicon-photonics-related systems—so growth in AI optics is not equivalent to a single fixed InP architecture winning every socket.

The sequence from committed demand to device-fab expansion, substrate investment and commercial epitaxy is stronger evidence of an industry capacity cycle than any one supplier's AI-demand forecast alone.

Japan is strengthening two distinct upstream layers of the InP photonics stack—substrates and epitaxy—but the public evidence does not establish that JX and Sumitomo are commercially linked or that Japan will capture downstream device value.
claims.basis: Supply-chain synthesis with explicit relationship boundary

claims.text: The main common-cause assumption is that hyperscale AI networking continues to require rapidly rising optical bandwidth; if that demand curve or architecture mix changes, today's synchronized capacity plans could become overbuild rather than confirmation of durable InP demand.

content.signal_score_note: ALAM internal analytical signal-strength score; it is not measured market share, adoption, utilization or probability.
evidence_for: FACT: March 2026 brought separate multiyear NVIDIA demand/capacity commitments with Coherent and Lumentum, plus $2 billion investments in each supplier.
FACT: Lumentum is adding a 6-inch InP manufacturing line with a stated mid-2028 ramp and NVIDIA as a customer.
FACT: Coherent's Sherman expansion is intended to quadruple wafer capacity, not merely add an R&D pilot line.
FACT: JX Advanced Metals plans up to ¥120 billion to raise Japanese InP substrate capacity roughly 7–10x versus FY2025.
FACT: Sumitomo Chemical has now moved 4-inch InP epitaxy into mass production and sales, adding a separate upstream manufacturing layer in Japan.
evidence_against: FACT: Sumitomo has not disclosed wafer volume, utilization, named customers, backlog, ASPs, qualification status or independent yield data.
FACT: Some of the largest capacity additions are future ramps rather than fully utilized output today; Lumentum's new 6-inch line is expected to ramp in mid-2028.
FACT: Coherent itself supports multiple optical architectures, so expanding AI optics does not guarantee the same InP content per link over time.

INFERENCE: The strongest demand evidence is concentrated around the same hyperscale AI spending cycle and major buyer ecosystem, so the observations are independent companies but not fully independent end-demand drivers.
content.connection: INFERENCE: The most plausible common cause is the bandwidth-and-power problem inside AI clusters. NVIDIA's purchase/capacity commitments show buyer-side urgency; Coherent and Lumentum are scaling device fabs; JX is expanding crystal substrates; Sumitomo has begun commercial epitaxy. These are different layers of one manufacturing chain, but there is no evidence here that all five parties share a direct commercial chain or that one supplier's demand proves another supplier's order book.
content.alternative_explanation: A synchronized capex wave can also be vendor herding around the same AI forecast, amplified by industrial-policy support and customer concentration. If hyperscaler capex slows, optical architectures reduce InP content, qualification takes longer than expected, or 6-inch economics pressure smaller-wafer production, today's capacity announcements could mature into excess supply rather than durable scarcity.
content.watch_next: Watch named multi-year design wins beyond the initial strategic agreements; Sumitomo production volume/utilization and customer qualification; JX's finalized investment tranches and pricing discussions; actual Coherent/Lumentum ramp milestones; InP wafer/epi lead times and pricing; and the architecture split among pluggable optics, silicon photonics, CPO, VCSEL-based solutions and other emerging approaches.
content.what_would_change_mind: Upgrade the trend if multiple independent customers disclose repeat production orders, utilization rises with scheduled ramps, supplier pricing remains firm despite added capacity, and 1.6T/3.2T/CPO deployments preserve or raise InP content. Downgrade it if announced fabs slip or cancel, utilization stays weak, qualification fails, prices collapse under excess capacity, or major AI networking roadmaps migrate materially toward architectures with less InP content.
content.implications: For semiconductor and equipment engineers, the durable opportunity is not one stock or one wafer size but the manufacturing stack: compound-semiconductor crystal growth, substrate quality, MOCVD epitaxy, uniformity/defect control, InP device fabrication, optical test/metrology, yield learning and photonic packaging. For Japan, JX + Sumitomo strengthen upstream capability, while the U.S. is scaling downstream 6-inch device capacity. Commercial winners will depend on qualification, yield, cost per good die and customer concentration—not announcement count.

reading_levels.30_sec: TREND: AI optics is no longer just a product-launch story. 2026 now has buyer commitments, 6-inch InP fab expansions, a 7–10x Japanese substrate plan, and commercial InP epiwafer production. Signal strength: 80/100 analytical score. Caveat: capacity commitment is not the same as profitable utilization, and competing optical architectures can reduce InP content.
reading_levels.2_min: The evidence spans separate companies and multiple manufacturing layers. NVIDIA committed multibillion-dollar purchasing/capacity agreements with Coherent and Lumentum; both suppliers are adding InP capacity. JX Advanced Metals plans up to ¥120B to lift Japanese InP substrate capacity roughly 7–10x FY2025, while Sumitomo Chemical has begun mass-producing and selling 4-inch InP epiwafers. That is enough to call a capacity cycle. But the same AI-networking demand thesis drives much of the spending, so this could still become overbuild if hyperscaler demand or optical architecture changes.
reading_levels.deep: The high-value checkpoints are manufacturing economics and qualification: substrate defectivity, epi uniformity, MOCVD throughput, device yield, wafer-size scaling, optical package yield, customer qualification and utilization. The trend becomes much stronger when new capacity converts into repeat orders and firm pricing; it weakens if ramps slip, utilization stays low or alternative architectures reduce InP content.

pr_vs_reality.official_claim: Suppliers and NVIDIA frame expanded advanced-optics and InP manufacturing as necessary infrastructure for scaling AI data centers and energy-efficient connectivity.
evidence_says: There are now real demand commitments and multiple capacity projects across substrates, epitaxy and device fabs.
Several projects are still future ramps, and Sumitomo has not disclosed volume, utilization or customer qualification.
The same AI demand cycle is a common cause across many announcements, and the optical architecture mix remains competitive.
pr_vs_reality.verdict: Real multi-layer capacity cycle, yes. Guaranteed shortage, guaranteed utilization, or guaranteed InP dominance, no.
